composio.note: Composio lists Slack under Composio-managed OAuth, so you can connect without your own app. Register your own Slack app for your own name/icon on the consent screen, custom bot/user scopes, or to keep the rate-limit and ToS relationship under your own app ID. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard when you create the auth config; Composio's own pages show different callback paths.

summary: Creating a Slack app and getting OAuth credentials takes minutes, and you can turn on public distribution yourself with no review. The catch: since 29 May 2025, commercially distributed apps that are not in the Slack Marketplace get conversations.history and conversations.replies cut to 1 request/minute and 15 messages per call, which hurts agents that read history. Getting into the Marketplace needs 10+ active workspace installs and a review that can take up to 10 weeks.
difficultyReason: The app itself is easy to set up (no review needed to distribute). The work is in the non-Marketplace rate limits on history reads and the long, strict Marketplace review needed to lift them.

time.notes: Unlisted public distribution has no review, but non-Marketplace apps get 1 req/min and 15 messages per call on conversations.history/replies. Marketplace review is up to 10 business days preliminary plus up to 10 weeks functional, after you reach 10 active installs; the total is inferred.

review.details: Single workspace: install directly, no review. Other workspaces: under Manage Distribution, complete the checklist and click 'Activate Public Distribution'. You do this yourself and Slack does not review it. Slack Marketplace listing (optional, but it lifts the non-Marketplace rate limits) is a human review: preliminary review within 10 business days, functional review up to 10 weeks for new apps, 10+ active workspaces required, plus a demo video and test credentials.

limitsBeforeApproval: Without Marketplace approval, an unlisted, commercially distributed app installs in any workspace, but new installs since 29 May 2025 get conversations.history/conversations.replies at Tier 1 (1 req/min) with a maximum of 15 objects per call. Internal, customer-built apps keep Tier 3 (50+/min, up to 1,000 objects). Workspace admins may still need to approve installs, depending on workspace settings.

prerequisites.item: A Slack workspace where you are allowed to create and install apps
prerequisites.why: Every app is created against a development workspace. Some orgs restrict app creation or require admin approval for installs.

prerequisites.item: Composio account and the redirect URI shown in the Composio auth-config screen
prerequisites.why: Slack only accepts redirect_uri values that match a registered Redirect URL (or a subpath of one).

prerequisites.item: Decision: bot scopes, user scopes, or both
prerequisites.why: Slack issues separate bot (xoxb) and user (xoxp) tokens from the scope and user_scope parameters. The Composio actions you plan to use decide which you need.

prerequisites.item: Public privacy policy, support page and landing page (Marketplace only)
prerequisites.why: Needed for a Marketplace listing, which is the only way to get the higher history limits for a commercially distributed app. Not needed for workspace-only or unlisted use.

steps.title: Pick scopes and draft an app manifest
steps.detail: Map the Composio Slack actions you need to the smallest set of bot/user scopes, then write a manifest (YAML/JSON) with the name, bot user, scopes and redirect URL. Leave out scopes for features you have not built; Marketplace review rejects them.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: At api.slack.com/apps click Create New App, choose 'From a manifest' (paste the draft) or 'From scratch', and pick the development workspace.

steps.title: Copy the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In Composio, go to Auth Configs > Create > Slack, choose your own credentials (not Composio Managed), and copy the redirect URI it shows. Do not copy it from docs; the documented values differ.

steps.title: Add Redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions, add the Composio redirect URI as a Redirect URL (HTTPS, no '#'). Add bot token scopes and/or user token scopes, then save.

steps.title: Copy Client ID and Client Secret into Composio
steps.detail: From Basic Information > App Credentials, paste the Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio auth config. Set the same scopes there, then save. Store the auth config ID (ac_...).

steps.title: Verify the configuration
steps.detail: Check that the redirect URI in Slack matches Composio's character for character (scheme, host, path), and that the scopes in Composio are a subset of those on the app. Then run a test connection and inspect the scopes on the returned token.

steps.title: Test-connect in your own workspace
steps.detail: Connect an account from Composio and approve the Slack consent screen. Confirm the connected account shows Active and a read/write action works.

steps.title: Activate public distribution (if other workspaces will connect)
steps.detail: Manage Distribution > complete the 'Share Your App with Other Workspaces' checklist > Activate Public Distribution. No Slack review. History-read limits for non-Marketplace apps apply from here on.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace submission materials (optional)
steps.detail: Draft listing copy, privacy policy text, a scope justification per scope, a test-account plan with dummy data, and a demo video script (install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use, uninstall).

steps.title: Submit to Slack Marketplace and get through review (optional)
steps.detail: Needs 10+ active workspaces (used in the past 28 days). Submit from app settings and answer reviewer feedback. Resubmitting during the preliminary stage resets your place in the queue.

nuances.title: History reads throttled for unlisted commercial apps
nuances.detail: From 29 May 2025, new unlisted apps and new installs of unlisted apps get conversations.history and conversations.replies at Tier 1 (1 req/min) and a maximum/default limit of 15. For an agent that summarises channels this is close to unusable. Internal customer-built apps are exempt.

nuances.title: Existing installs: enforcement date unclear
nuances.detail: The original changelog says existing installs are unaffected. Search results quote Slack pages that move existing installs onto the new limits on 3 March 2026 (earlier: 2 September 2025). I could not confirm this on a page I fetched.

nuances.title: 'Internal' vs 'commercially distributed' is not precisely defined
nuances.detail: The fetched clarification only says internal customer-built apps keep their limits. If your agent product installs your app in customer workspaces, assume it counts as commercially distributed.

nuances.title: Redirect URI matching allows subpaths
nuances.detail: The redirect_uri must match a configured Redirect URL or be a subdirectory of it. Scheme, host and port must match exactly. With several Redirect URLs, send the same redirect_uri in both the authorize and access calls, or Slack returns bad_redirect_uri.

nuances.title: Marketplace review rejects broad or speculative scopes
nuances.detail: Scopes such as admin.*, search:read, client, read and post, plus scopes for unbuilt features, are listed as reasons for rejection. Request only what current features use.

nuances.title: API Terms of Service were updated alongside the rate-limit change
nuances.detail: Updated API ToS took effect immediately for apps created on or after 29 May 2025. Review the data-use terms if your agent stores or indexes Slack messages. I did not read the ToS text itself.

blockers.problem: Agent reads of channel history are capped at 1 request/min and 15 messages
blockers.whatToDo: Either keep the app internal to one customer's workspace (each customer registers their own app), get listed in the Slack Marketplace, or use the Composio-managed app and check its limits with Composio.

blockers.problem: Not eligible for Marketplace yet (fewer than 10 active workspaces)
blockers.whatToDo: Distribute unlisted to design partners first. Note that those installs run under the reduced limits until listing.

blockers.problem: Workspace blocks app installs or requires admin approval
blockers.whatToDo: Ask a workspace admin to approve the app. Keep scopes minimal to make approval easier.
Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard again and make it identical in Slack (https, same host and path).

agentCanDo: Map the Composio Slack actions you need to a minimal set of bot and user scopes
Generate the app manifest (name, bot user, scopes, redirect URL) to paste into 'Create from manifest'
Compare the Slack Redirect URL with the URI shown in Composio and flag mismatches
Run a test connection through the Composio API and report which scopes were granted
Draft privacy policy, listing copy, scope justifications and a demo-video script for Marketplace submission
Check the Slack changelog for current rate-limit rules for non-Marketplace apps
developerMustDo: Sign in to Slack and create the app in a workspace they control
Copy the client secret into Composio, which needs an authenticated session in both consoles
Approve the OAuth consent screen during the test connection
Click Activate Public Distribution and accept Slack's API terms
Get 10+ real workspace installs, record the demo, provide test credentials and submit to the Marketplace
redirectUri: Must use HTTPS and cannot contain '#'. The redirect_uri sent at runtime must match a registered Redirect URL or be a subpath of one; scheme, host and port must match exactly. I did not find official guidance on http://localhost; assume HTTPS only. For Composio, paste the exact callback URI shown when you create the Slack auth config with your own credentials. Composio docs show https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback, a v3.1 variant and an older .../api/v1/auth-apps/add, so the dashboard value is the one to trust.

sources.title: Slack: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps (2025-05-29)
Slack: Clarifying rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps (2025-06-03)

claims.claim: New unlisted, commercially distributed apps and new installs of them get conversations.history/replies at Tier 1 (1 req/min) with a maximum/default limit of 15, effective 29 May 2025.
Internal customer-built apps are not affected and keep 50+ req/min with up to 1,000 objects per call.
Existing installs of unlisted apps moved onto the reduced limits on 3 March 2026.
Redirect URLs and redirect_uri must use HTTPS. redirect_uri may be a subdirectory of a configured URL. Scheme, host and port must match.
Public (unlisted) distribution is activated by the developer from Manage Distribution, with no Slack review step described.
Marketplace review: preliminary review up to 10 business days, functional review up to 10 weeks for new submissions, and it cannot be expedited.
Marketplace submission needs the app installed on 10+ active workspaces (active = used in the past 28 days), plus test credentials and a demo video.
Undistributed apps can only be installed in the workspace where they were created.
Composio offers a managed OAuth app for Slack.

openQuestions: Did Slack actually enforce the reduced history limits on existing unlisted installs (reported date 3 March 2026)? The conversations.history reference page I fetched still shows only Tier 3.
Is an app that each customer registers in their own workspace (bring-your-own Slack app per customer) treated as 'internal customer-built' and exempt from the limits?
Does the Composio-managed Slack app have Marketplace status, and so Tier 3 history limits?

Which redirect URI does Composio currently issue: .../api/v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback, .../api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (shown in composio.dev/auth guides), or the older .../api/v1/auth-apps/add? Copy it from the dashboard.
Does Slack accept http://localhost Redirect URLs for local testing? Not covered in the OAuth doc I fetched.
